boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Drew University
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night dining spots and campus rituals for students at Drew University, focusing on under-21-safe options available after dark.

cards.title: The C-Store at McLendon Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Convenience Hub
cards.notes: Visit the first floor of McLendon Hall for late-night snacks and hot food. It is a primary social and dining hub for students after main dining halls close.
cards.short_summary: A campus convenience store in McLendon Hall offering hot meals and snacks until 2:00 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: The convenience store, or C-store, is located right next to McLendon Hall and is opened from 6 p.m. to 2 a.m. every night.
cards.source_title: Inside the Life at the C-Store - The Drew Acorn
cards.access_notes: Open nightly from 6:00 PM to 2:00 AM.

cards.title: Late Night at The Commons
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Dining Hall
cards.notes: Head to the main dining hall for late-night meal sessions. It serves as a central gathering point for students to eat and study together in the evenings.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus dining hall offering late-night hours for students on meal plans.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons closes at 8:30 p.m., and the E.C. closes at 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: Inside the Life at the C-Store - The Drew Acorn
cards.access_notes: Main dining hours typically end at 8:30 PM.

cards.title: Ehinger Center Food Court
cards.subtitle: Student Center Dining
cards.notes: Stop by the EC for a variety of food options including pizza and burgers. It remains open later than the main dining hall for evening cravings.
cards.short_summary: A multi-vendor food court in the student center featuring Yella's and Lil' Anthony's Pizza.
cards.evidence_claim: The E.C. closes at 10 p.m., so after 10, the C-store can often be packed with people.
cards.source_title: Inside the Life at the C-Store - The Drew Acorn
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 10:00 PM.

cards.title: The Halal Shack at Drew
cards.subtitle: Mediterranean Campus Eats
cards.notes: Order Mediterranean-style bowls and wraps through the Grubhub app. This spot provides a flavorful late-evening alternative to standard dining hall fare.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining location in the Ehinger Center serving Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine.
cards.evidence_claim: The EC food court now includes... the Halal Shack's Mediterranean gyros and falafels.
cards.source_title: A Look at Drew's New Campus Dining
cards.access_notes: Located within the Ehinger Center; hours follow the food court schedule.

cards.title: Yella's at the EC
cards.subtitle: Burgers and Milkshakes
cards.notes: Grab a signature milkshake or burger at this EC food court staple. It is a popular choice for students looking for a treat during late-night study breaks.
cards.short_summary: A campus eatery in the Ehinger Center known for burgers, sandwiches, and hand-spun milkshakes.
cards.evidence_claim: The EC food court now includes Yella's sandwiches, salads, burgers, and milkshakes.
cards.source_title: A Look at Drew's New Campus Dining
cards.access_notes: Operates during Ehinger Center food court hours.

cards.title: Nautilus Diner
cards.subtitle: Classic Madison Landmark
cards.notes: Walk or drive to this local landmark for late-night breakfast and Greek specialties. It offers extended hours on weekends for off-campus dining runs.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Madison diner located near campus, offering a large menu and late-night weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Operating Hours: Friday: 7AM-10PM | Saturday: 7AM-10PM.
cards.source_title: Nautilus Diner - Morris County Economic Development Alliance
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM on Fridays and Saturdays.

cards.title: Wawa on Route 124
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Convenience Run
cards.notes: Drive to the nearby Wawa for 24-hour access to hoagies and coffee. It is a reliable destination for students when all on-campus options have closed.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store and gas station located a short drive from the Drew campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Our stores are always open, bright, clean, warm and welcoming.
cards.source_title: Locations - Wawa
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: 7-Eleven Florham Park
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Snack Stop
cards.notes: Visit this 24/7 spot for quick snacks and drinks. Located just a few miles from campus, it serves as a frequent stop for late-night supply runs.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store located near the Drew University campus in Florham Park.
cards.evidence_claim: 7-Eleven at 151 Columbia Turnpike Florham Park, NJ 07932... Open 24/7.
cards.source_title: 6 River Rd Summit NJ 07901 - 7-Eleven
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Dunkin' on Main Street
cards.subtitle: Evening Coffee & Donuts
cards.notes: Stop by for a late-evening coffee or donut before the shop closes. It is located on Main Street, within walking distance for many students.
cards.short_summary: A popular coffee and donut shop in downtown Madison with evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: 227 Main St. Madison, NJ 07940... Open Now Closes at 8:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' at 227 Main St in Madison | Coffee & Donuts Near You
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 8:00 PM.

cards.title: PJs & Pancakes Late Night
cards.subtitle: Finals Week Tradition
cards.notes: Attend this special late-night breakfast event during finals week. It is a major campus tradition where students gather for pancakes and community support.
cards.short_summary: A recurring late-night breakfast event held in The Commons during exam periods.
cards.evidence_claim: Wednesday, May 6 | PJs & Pancakes Late Night Breakfast | 10 p.m.-1 a.m. in The Commons.
cards.source_title: Commencement Information - Drew University
cards.access_notes: Special event hours, typically 10:00 PM to 1:00 AM during finals.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student hubs and quiet retreats across The Forest that define daily life at Drew University beyond the standard admissions route.

cards.title: Silent Study in the Kean Room
cards.subtitle: Rose Memorial Library, Level C
cards.notes: Visit Level C for a strictly enforced silent zone. It is ideal for deep focus sessions when the main library commons becomes too social for heavy academic work.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent study zone located on Level C of the Rose Memorial Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kean Room on Level C is designated as a silent zone for individual study.
cards.source_title: Find Your Zone | Silent, Quiet, Social and Hybrid
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; accessible to students with a valid Drew ID.

cards.title: Relax at the 1867 Lounge
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center
cards.notes: Head to the EC to find this lounge filled with comfortable chairs. It is a central spot to relax between classes or meet up with friends near the dining area.
cards.short_summary: A central student lounge located within the Ehinger Center featuring comfortable seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The 1867 Lounge is located in the Ehinger Center where students can relax and work in comfy chairs.
cards.source_title: Campus Event Spaces and Documentation
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Ehinger Center; typically open during building operating hours.

cards.title: Nature Retreat at Zuck Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Drew Forest Preserve
cards.notes: Walk the self-guided trails around the glacial ponds. It serves as a quiet woodland retreat for passive recreation and observing local wildlife like turtles and herons.
cards.short_summary: A 45-acre forest preserve on campus featuring glacial ponds and nature trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zuck Arboretum is open for passive recreation and serves as a woodland retreat with a self-guiding nature trail around its ponds.
cards.source_title: Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration at Drew
cards.access_notes: Trails are open to the public; visitors must close gates to protect the ecosystem from deer.

cards.title: The Commuter Hub
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center
cards.notes: Utilize the recently renovated space featuring a full-sized refrigerator, microwave, and foosball table. It is the primary social anchor for non-resident students.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge for commuter students in the Ehinger Center with kitchen amenities and social games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commuter Lounge in the Ehinger Center features a large refrigerator, microwave, coffee machine, and foosball table.
cards.source_title: The Commuters Lounge Finally Reopens!
cards.access_notes: Primarily for commuter students; located within the Ehinger Center.

cards.title: Laps at the Simon Forum Pool
cards.subtitle: Simon Forum & Athletic Center
cards.notes: Access the eight-lane, 25-yard NCAA pool for open swim hours. Remember to bring your Drew ID for entry at the Baldwin Gym Patio entrance.
cards.short_summary: An indoor NCAA-regulation swimming pool available for use by the Drew community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simon Forum houses an eight-lane 25-yard NCAA pool open for the Drew community.
cards.source_title: Simon Forum Hours
cards.access_notes: Valid Drew ID required for entry; check seasonal hours for open swim times.

cards.title: Historic Steps of Mead Hall
cards.subtitle: Mead Hall Entrance
cards.notes: Sit on the thick stone steps of the Greek Revival mansion. It is the historic heart of campus and a quiet spot for outdoor reading under the massive Ionic columns.
cards.short_summary: The grand entrance portico of the historic 1836 Mead Hall mansion.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Hall features a full-height portico with six massive Ionic columns and ten thick stone steps.
cards.source_title: A Walk Through Mead Hall
cards.access_notes: Outdoor piazza is publicly accessible; interior houses administrative offices.

cards.title: Performances at The Space
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center
cards.notes: Check the schedule for student-led coffee house events. This informal venue hosts comedians, poets, and musicians in a relaxed, creative environment.
cards.short_summary: An informal performance venue in the Ehinger Center for student creative expression.
cards.evidence_claim: The Space is a campus venue where comedians, poets, and musicians often perform in a coffee house style.
cards.source_title: Event Rentals & Facilities
cards.access_notes: Open during scheduled events and building hours.

cards.title: Global Hub at Tilghman House
cards.subtitle: Tilghman House
cards.notes: Visit this center for cultural programming and international student support. It provides a dedicated lobby and meeting space for the global student community.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated center for international student services and cultural exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Tilghman International Center provides a place for students and hosts educational and cultural programs.
cards.source_title: International Student & Scholar Services
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; primary hub for international student advising.

cards.title: Practical Needs at Pepin
cards.subtitle: Pepin Services Building
cards.notes: Go here to replace a lost ID card or borrow a shovel during snowstorms. It houses the Service Response Center and Public Safety desk for essential campus help.
cards.short_summary: The administrative hub for campus facilities, ID services, and public safety.
cards.evidence_claim: The Service Response Center in the Pepin Services Center handles ID card replacements and loans shovels to students.
cards.source_title: Facilities Management FAQs
cards.access_notes: Service Response Center open Mon-Fri 7:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Public Safety open 24/7.

cards.title: Casual Reading on the Couches
cards.subtitle: Rose Memorial Library, Level E
cards.notes: Climb the main stairs and turn left to find these comfortable couches. They offer a great vantage point for people-watching while catching up on light reading.
cards.short_summary: A casual study area with comfortable seating on the upper level of the library.
cards.evidence_claim: The second-story library couches are a popular spot for reading and observing the library entrance.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Best Study Spots at Drew
cards.access_notes: Accessible during library operating hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore the best of Drew University and Madison without spending a dime. From serene forest trails and historic architecture to late-night student events and art galleries, these campus and local spots offer free social and recreational opportunities for every student.

cards.title: Hike the Forest Trails
cards.subtitle: Nature trails behind the athletic fields
cards.notes: Explore 45 acres of native woodland and glacial ponds. The trails are open to the public and students for birdwatching and quiet walks through the 'Forest'.
cards.short_summary: A 45-acre natural woodland on campus featuring diverse bird species and ecological restoration sites.
cards.evidence_claim: The Drew Forest Preserve trails are open to the public and include a self-guiding nature trail around the ponds.
cards.source_title: Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration at Drew
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk; enter through the gates near the baseball outfield and close them behind you.

cards.title: Relax by the Ponds
cards.subtitle: South end of campus
cards.notes: Visit the two small ponds within the arboretum for a peaceful study break. It serves as a natural laboratory and a quiet retreat for the community.
cards.short_summary: A serene arboretum featuring two ponds that serve as a natural laboratory and a woodland retreat.
cards.evidence_claim: The arboretum and its two small ponds serve as natural laboratories and a woodland retreat with free admission.
cards.source_title: Florence & Robert Zuck Arboretum | VisitNJ.org
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Drew Forest Preserve trails; open during daylight hours.

cards.title: View Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Dorothy Young Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Browse rotating exhibitions featuring professional artists and student work. The gallery hosts about six shows a year with free admission for all.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery presenting diverse exhibitions, including student shows and artist-in-residence projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Korn Gallery is open Tuesday through Friday, 12-4pm, and offers free admission to its exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Explore Inspiring Art at Korn Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Friday 12:00 PM - 4:00 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Tour Historic Mead Hall
cards.subtitle: The administrative core of campus
cards.notes: Walk through this 1833 Greek Revival mansion. While it houses offices, the main hall and architecture are open for self-guided appreciation.
cards.short_summary: An iconic 19th-century Greek Revival building that serves as the symbolic heart of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Hall is a working university building with offices and meeting rooms, and its architecture is a focal point for the community.
cards.source_title: A Walk Through Mead Hall
cards.access_notes: Open during standard university business hours, typically Monday-Friday 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Join Friday Night Events
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center (EC)
cards.notes: Attend free late-night social events every Friday starting at 8pm. Activities include games, crafts, and themed mixers for all students.
cards.short_summary: A student-led program providing free late-night social activities on Friday evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Drew Night Life plans late night events every Friday night starting at 8pm in the Ehinger Center.
cards.source_title: Student Activities | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Events typically begin at 8:00 PM on Fridays in the Ehinger Center.

cards.entity_name: United Methodist Archives and History Center
cards.title: Research Global History
cards.subtitle: Across from Rose Memorial Library
cards.notes: Access one of the world's largest collections of Methodist history. The Wilson Reading Room is open to students and visitors for free research.
cards.short_summary: A major archival center housing extensive records of United Methodism and university history.
cards.evidence_claim: The materials held in The United Methodist Archives and History Center are available to anyone interested in viewing them for free.
cards.source_title: United Methodist Archives and History Center
cards.access_notes: Reading room open Monday-Friday 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM; non-Drew visitors require an appointment.

cards.title: Swim or Play Squash
cards.subtitle: Campus athletic complex
cards.notes: Use your student ID to access the 25-yard pool, indoor track, and racquetball courts. Most campus recreation services are free for students.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic facility on campus offering a pool, fitness rooms, and various sports courts.
cards.evidence_claim: Most campus services and events, including access to the Simon Forum, are free for Drew students.
cards.source_title: Commuter Students | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; valid Drew ID required for entry.

cards.title: Attend Free Concerts
cards.subtitle: Music Department performances
cards.notes: Enjoy free performances by the Drew Orchestra, Jazz Ensemble, and Flute Ensemble. Most end-of-semester recitals are open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A venue for high-quality musical performances by student ensembles and faculty, often free to attend.
cards.evidence_claim: Drew University celebrates the end of the semester with musical performances that are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Drew University Announces Free Musical Performances
cards.access_notes: Concerts typically held in the evenings; check the university calendar for specific dates.

cards.title: Join Library Programs
cards.subtitle: 39 Keep Street, Madison
cards.notes: Participate in free workshops, book clubs, and film screenings just a short walk from campus. A local library card is free for residents.
cards.short_summary: The local public library offering a variety of free educational and cultural programs for the community.
cards.evidence_claim: Most programs for children, teens, and adults offered by the library are sponsored by the Friends and are free.
cards.source_title: Events Calendar - Madison Public Library
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM, Friday-Saturday 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Hang Out in the EC
cards.subtitle: Student Union building
cards.notes: Relax in the Commuter Lounge or the main student hub. It's a central spot for meeting friends, playing pool, or studying between classes.
cards.short_summary: The heart of student life on campus, featuring lounges, meeting spaces, and recreational facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The EC is a gathering place for students, staff, and faculty, offering a variety of free resources and facilities.
cards.source_title: The Ehinger Center | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; hours may vary during breaks.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From signing a 150-year-old ledger to planting native ferns in the heart of campus, Drew University's traditions are deeply rooted in its wooded environment and Methodist history.

cards.title: Signing the 150-Year-Old Ledger
cards.subtitle: A rite of passage for new scholars
cards.notes: Join generations of Drewids by signing the historic matriculation book in Craig Chapel, a tradition dating back to the school's 1867 founding.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students formally enter the university community by signing a historic ledger that dates back to 1867.
cards.evidence_claim: The matriculation book signing is a 150-year-old tradition for all incoming students, linking them to generations of Drew scholars.
cards.source_title: Drew Theological School DMin Students Sign Matriculation Book
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the Fall Matriculation Service in Craig Chapel for new students.

cards.title: The Annual Reforestation
cards.subtitle: Planting native ferns in the Forest
cards.notes: Celebrate Earth Day by planting native ferns and wildflowers to restore the campus ecosystem under the university's majestic oaks.
cards.short_summary: An annual Earth Day event where students and faculty plant native vegetation to maintain the university's 'Forest' identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Fern Fest is an annual event where students replenish native ferns and wildflowers to protect the campus ecosystem.
cards.source_title: Fern Fest Returns After Two-Year Hiatus - The Drew Acorn
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April near the center of campus.

cards.title: The Senior Countdown
cards.subtitle: Celebrating 99 days to graduation
cards.notes: Seniors gather exactly 99 nights before commencement to toast their time at Drew and begin the final countdown to graduation.
cards.short_summary: A milestone celebration for seniors held 99 days before their graduation ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: 99 Nights is a tradition where seniors celebrate the 99th night before graduation, kicking off the countdown to Commencement.
cards.source_title: Discover Rich Traditions at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Exclusive to the senior class; typically held in the Ehinger Center.

cards.title: The Renaissance Shindig
cards.subtitle: Medieval revelry at Bowne Hall
cards.notes: Step back to the 13th century with human chess, turkey legs, and knighting ceremonies in the shadow of the castle-like S.W. Bowne Hall.
cards.short_summary: A medieval-themed festival featuring period-accurate games, food, and performances organized by 'That Medieval Thing'.
cards.evidence_claim: MedFest is an annual Renaissance-style festival featuring human chess and knighting ceremonies at S.W. Bowne Hall.
cards.source_title: Discover Rich Traditions at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; held annually in the spring near S.W. Bowne Hall.

cards.title: A Cappella Harmony Night
cards.subtitle: The ultimate vocal showcase
cards.notes: Experience the harmony of Drew's three a cappella groups—36 Madison Ave, All of the Above, and On a Different Note—in one massive concert.
cards.short_summary: A major semester-end concert featuring all of the university's student-run a cappella ensembles.
cards.evidence_claim: JamFest is a single-night event that unites all of Drew's a cappella groups for a major performance.
cards.source_title: 36 Madison Avenue Celebrates 36 Years of A Capella - The Drew Acorn
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Dorothy Young Center for the Arts or the Ehinger Center.

cards.title: The Ranger Pitch
cards.subtitle: Student business ideas on stage
cards.notes: Watch students pitch business ideas to a panel of alumni and experts in this semi-annual competition, formerly known as Shark Tank.
cards.short_summary: An entrepreneurial competition where students present product ideas for feedback and potential funding.
cards.evidence_claim: Bear Den, formerly Shark Tank, is a semi-annual event where students pitch business ideas to faculty and alumni.
cards.source_title: Discover Rich Traditions at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Held in the Ehinger Center; open to student spectators.

cards.title: The Final Vigil
cards.subtitle: A glowing farewell to the Forest
cards.notes: Gather by candlelight on the night before graduation to reflect on your time in the Forest and prepare for the world beyond.
cards.short_summary: A reflective, candlelit gathering for graduating seniors held on the eve of commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The Senior Ceremony is held the night before graduation, where students gather by candlelight to mark their time at Drew.
cards.source_title: Discover Rich Traditions at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Exclusive to the graduating class; held outdoors on the campus grounds.

cards.title: The High-Energy Arrival
cards.subtitle: Upperclassmen hauling your gear
cards.notes: Experience the roar of the Welcome Crew as they cheer for every car and carry your belongings to your new dorm room.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy move-in tradition where student volunteers assist new arrivals with their luggage and gear.
cards.evidence_claim: On Move-In Day, the Drew Welcome Crew erupts into cheers and helps new students carry their belongings to their rooms.
cards.source_title: Discover Rich Traditions at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Occurs on the official new student move-in day in August.

cards.title: The Formal Holiday Gala
cards.subtitle: Cocktail attire and cider fountains
cards.notes: Dress up for the annual formal dance featuring chocolate fountains, cookie decorating, and a winter wonderland transformation of the EC.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing formal holiday dance for the entire student body, traditionally known as the Holiday Ball.
cards.evidence_claim: The Winter Ball (formerly Holiday Ball) is a long-standing tradition where students dress in cocktail attire for a festive evening.
cards.source_title: Students Have a Ball at Winter Ball - The Drew Acorn
cards.access_notes: Held in December at the Ehinger Center; tickets required.

cards.title: The Alumni Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Rangers returning to the Forest
cards.notes: Celebrate school spirit with alumni games, the Hall of Fame ceremony, and varsity doubleheaders at Ranger Stadium.
cards.short_summary: The university's athletic homecoming weekend featuring alumni reunions and major sporting events.
cards.evidence_claim: Ranger Weekend is a yearly tradition of welcoming alumni back to the Forest for athletic games and ceremonies.
cards.source_title: Ranger Weekend to be Held Oct. 18-19 - Drew University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Held annually in October; events take place across various athletic facilities.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Drew University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack in The Forest
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned residence hall during your morning time slot to begin your transition into the Drew community.
cards.short_summary: The official start of the fall semester for new first-year and transfer students.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Move-in for Fall 2026 takes place on the morning of Friday, August 28, with assigned times based on housing.
cards.source_title: Experience Fall Orientation at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Required for all new residential students; check your Drew email for specific building assignments.

cards.title: Formal Welcome to Campus
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Tradition
cards.notes: Join faculty and staff for this formal induction ceremony that marks the official start of your academic journey.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial welcome for new students and their families held on move-in Friday.
cards.evidence_claim: The Opening of School Ceremony is held on the afternoon of August 28, 2026, where faculty and staff formally welcome the community.
cards.source_title: Experience Fall Orientation at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and their families; typically held in a central campus location.

cards.title: Grab a Bite at the EC
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Social
cards.notes: Visit the campus hub for dinner and explore the 1867 Lounge or the various food options like pizza and pasta.
cards.short_summary: The central student union and gathering place located between residences and academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ehinger Center (EC) serves as a gathering place with dining options including pizza, pasta, and a Starbucks.
cards.source_title: The Ehinger Center | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; dining hours vary by station. Student ID required for meal plans.

cards.title: Friday Night Fun
cards.subtitle: Late Night Programming
cards.notes: Head back to the EC for late-night activities designed to help you meet fellow students in a relaxed environment.
cards.short_summary: Weekly late-night social events hosted by the Office of Student Activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Drew Night Life plans late night events every Friday night starting at 8pm in the Ehinger Center.
cards.source_title: Student Activities | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Events typically begin at 8:00 PM on Friday nights during the semester.

cards.title: Morning Walk in the Woods
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Nature
cards.notes: Explore the self-guiding nature trail around the ponds to spot turtles and local bird species in the Forest Preserve.
cards.short_summary: A 45-acre natural laboratory and woodland retreat located on the south side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zuck Arboretum features trails open to the public, including a self-guiding nature trail around the ponds.
cards.source_title: Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration at Drew
cards.access_notes: Trails are open to the public; enter through the gates near the baseball fields and lift the latch.

cards.title: Active Afternoon
cards.subtitle: Saturday Fitness Session
cards.notes: Use your student ID to access the fitness room, weight room, or the 200-meter indoor track for a workout.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic facility on campus, housing a pool, gym, and fitness centers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simon Forum facilities are open for the Drew community and require a valid Drew ID for entry.
cards.source_title: Simon Forum and Athletic Center | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Academic year hours: Mon-Fri 8am-10pm, Sat 10am-7pm, Sun 12pm-6pm.

cards.title: Explore the Rose City
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Out
cards.notes: Walk five minutes from campus to Main Street to browse local shops and grab a coffee or ice cream.
cards.short_summary: The historic and safe downtown area of Madison, NJ, located just steps from the university gates.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Madison is a five-minute walk from campus and features cafes, restaurants, and shops along Main Street.
cards.source_title: Discover Madison – Your Home Beyond the Forest
cards.access_notes: Easily accessible via the Lancaster Road entrance; most shops close by 6:00 PM or 8:00 PM.

cards.title: Find Your Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Prep
cards.notes: Scope out the silent study areas on the second floor or reserve a group study room for upcoming projects.
cards.short_summary: The main university library offering diverse study environments from social to silent.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose Memorial Library offers group study spaces, private day carrels, and designated silent study zones.
cards.source_title: Find Your Zone | Silent, Quiet, Social and Hybrid
cards.access_notes: Current Drew ID required for entry during late-night study hours.

cards.title: Visit the Historic Heart
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon History
cards.notes: Admire the Greek Revival architecture of Drew's original 1836 building, now serving as the administrative core.
cards.short_summary: A National Register of Historic Places mansion that is the symbolic center of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Hall is the original building on the Drew site, built in 1832-1836, and remains a focal point for the community.
cards.source_title: Mead Hall - Drew University
cards.access_notes: Primarily houses offices; the exterior and main hall are accessible during business hours.

cards.title: Catch a Performance
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Culture
cards.notes: Check for student rush tickets or 'Under 35' discounts to see professional theatre right on campus.
cards.short_summary: An independent professional theatre company residency located on the Drew University campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey offers $35 tickets for those under 35 and student discounts for performances.
cards.source_title: Ways To Save | Shakespeare NJ
cards.access_notes: Box office opens 12:00 PM on performance days; check the seasonal calendar for showtimes.
